API reference¶

The news app¶

The news app: articles, newsletters, publishers and subscriptions.

Readers follow publishers and journalists, journalists write articles and newsletters, and editors review and approve articles. Approval logic lives in news.services and API access rules in news.permissions.

Models¶

Database models for the news application.

Tables are normalised: each entity (user, publisher, article, newsletter, approval log) lives in its own table, and relationships use foreign keys and many-to-many join tables instead of repeated columns.

Services (approval flow)¶

Business logic for approving articles (Option 2: no signals).

The approval view (web and API) calls approve_article(), which marks the article approved, emails subscribers and posts the article to the internal /api/approved/ endpoint.

news.services.get_subscriber_emails(article)[source]¶

Return the emails of readers subscribed to an article’s source.

A reader is included if they follow the article’s journalist or its publisher. Readers without an email address are skipped.

Parameters:

article (Article) – The article whose subscribers are wanted.

Returns:

Unique email addresses, sorted alphabetically. Empty if the article has neither an author nor a publisher.

Return type:

list[str]

news.services.email_subscribers(article)[source]¶

Email the approved article to its subscribers.

Subscribers are sent the article by Bcc so their addresses stay private. Mail errors are logged, not raised, so a mail outage never blocks an approval.

Parameters:

article (Article) – The approved article to send.

Returns:

The number of recipients, or 0 if there were none or the email could not be sent.

Return type:

int

news.services.post_to_approved_api(article, editor)[source]¶

POST the approved article to the /api/approved/ endpoint.

The request is authenticated with the approving editor’s API token, which is created if the editor does not have one yet. Network and HTTP errors are logged, not raised.

Parameters:

  • article (Article) – The approved article to log.

  • editor (CustomUser) – The editor who approved the article.

Returns:

True if the endpoint accepted the article, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

news.services.approve_article(article, editor)[source]¶

Approve article as editor and share it.

The article is marked approved and stamped with the editor and the time. Once the database transaction commits, subscribers are emailed and the article is posted to /api/approved/.

Parameters:

  • article (Article) – The article to approve.

  • editor (CustomUser) – The user approving the article.

Returns:

The updated, approved article.

Return type:

Article

Raises:

  • PermissionError – If editor does not have the Editor role.

  • ValueError – If the article has already been approved.

news.services._share_article(article, editor)[source]¶

Email subscribers and log the article at /api/approved/.

Parameters:

  • article (Article) – The newly approved article.

  • editor (CustomUser) – The editor who approved it.

Permissions¶

Role-based permission classes for the REST API.

Each class is used by a view in news.api_views. Django REST Framework calls has_permission for every request and has_object_permission when a single object is retrieved, updated or deleted.

class news.permissions.ArticlePermission[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Control access to articles by role.

  • Any signed-in user may view articles.

  • Only journalists may create articles.

  • Editors may update or delete any article; journalists only their own.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Check the caller’s role for the request method.

has_object_permission(request, view, obj)[source]¶

Editors may change any article; journalists only their own.

class news.permissions.NewsletterPermission[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Control access to newsletters by role.

  • Any signed-in user may view newsletters.

  • Journalists and editors may create newsletters.

  • The newsletter’s author or an editor may update or delete it.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Anyone signed in may read; journalists and editors may write.

has_object_permission(request, view, obj)[source]¶

Editors may change any newsletter; others only their own.

class news.permissions.IsEditor[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Allow only signed-in users with the Editor role.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Return True for authenticated editors.

class news.permissions.IsReader[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Allow only signed-in users with the Reader role.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Return True for authenticated readers.

Web views¶

Web views for the news application.

Every view that changes data checks the user’s role (through role_required()) and, where relevant, whether the user owns the object (through the can_modify_* helpers).

news.views.role_required(*roles)[source]¶

Decorator: allow only signed-in users whose role is in roles.

Anonymous users are redirected to the login page; signed-in users with another role get a 403 Forbidden response.

Example:

@role_required(Role.EDITOR)
def review_queue(request):
    ...
Parameters:

*roles (str) – The Role values allowed to use the view.

Returns:

A decorator that wraps a view function.

Return type:

Callable

news.views.can_modify_article(user, article)[source]¶

Return True if user may edit or delete article.

Editors may change any article; journalists only their own.

news.views.can_modify_newsletter(user, newsletter)[source]¶

Return True if user may edit or delete newsletter.

Editors may change any newsletter; journalists only their own.

news.views.can_create_publisher(user)[source]¶

Return True if user may create publishers.

Any editor, or a site administrator (superuser), may do so.

news.views.can_manage_publisher(user, publisher)[source]¶

Return True if user may edit or delete publisher.

Superusers may manage every publisher. Editors may manage the publishers they are an editor of.

news.views.register(request)[source]¶

Show the sign-up form and log the new user in on success.

The chosen role puts the user in the matching group (see CustomUser.save()).

news.views.home(request)[source]¶

List approved articles, newest first, with optional search.

?q= filters by title or content; ?page= paginates.

news.views.article_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Show one article.

Guests and readers see only approved articles. Journalists may also see their own pending articles, and editors may see every article.

news.views.article_create(request)[source]¶

Let a journalist write a new article (journalists only).

The article is saved unapproved and goes to the editors’ review queue. With no publisher selected it is an independent article; the form sets the journalist as author before validation so this works.

news.views.article_update(request, pk)[source]¶

Edit an article (its author, or any editor).

news.views.article_delete(request, pk)[source]¶

Confirm (GET) and delete (POST) an article (its author or an editor).

news.views.my_articles(request)[source]¶

List the signed-in journalist’s articles, including pending ones.

news.views.review_queue(request)[source]¶

List every article still waiting for approval (editors only).

news.views.article_approve(request, pk)[source]¶

Approve an article (editors only, POST only).

Delegates to news.services.approve_article(), which emails subscribers and POSTs the article to /api/approved/.

news.views.newsletter_list(request)[source]¶

List all newsletters (public).

news.views.newsletter_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Show a newsletter and its approved articles (public).

news.views.newsletter_create(request)[source]¶

Create a newsletter (journalists and editors). The signed-in user becomes its author.

news.views.newsletter_update(request, pk)[source]¶

Edit a newsletter (its author, or any editor).

news.views.newsletter_delete(request, pk)[source]¶

Confirm (GET) and delete (POST) a newsletter (its author or an editor).

news.views.publisher_list(request)[source]¶

List all publishers (public). Editors also see a “New publisher” button.

news.views.publisher_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Show a publisher with its staff and approved articles.

Readers get a Subscribe button; the publisher’s editors get Manage and Delete buttons.

news.views.publisher_create(request)[source]¶

Create a publisher and pick its editors and journalists.

Open to editors and superusers. An editor who creates a publisher is always added to its editors so they can manage it afterwards.

news.views.publisher_update(request, pk)[source]¶

Edit a publisher’s details and its editors and journalists.

Open to the publisher’s own editors and to superusers.

news.views.publisher_delete(request, pk)[source]¶

Confirm (GET) and delete (POST) a publisher.

Open to the publisher’s own editors and to superusers. Its articles are kept and become independent (on_delete=SET_NULL).

news.views.journalist_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Show a journalist’s profile and approved articles, with a Subscribe button for readers.

news.views.toggle_subscription(request, kind, pk)[source]¶

Subscribe to, or unsubscribe from, a publisher or journalist.

kind is 'publisher' or 'journalist'. Readers only.

news.views.my_subscriptions(request)[source]¶

Show a reader’s subscriptions and the approved articles from them.

API views¶

REST API views.

Access is enforced by the permission classes in news.permissions; every endpoint requires token (or session) authentication.

news.api_views.visible_articles(user)[source]¶

Return the articles user may see.

Everyone sees approved articles. Editors also see all pending ones, and journalists see their own pending ones.
